issues.title: False boundary limits in the multivariate VG critical case trichotomy
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local correction of the limit case analysis; the derived domain-transformation rule, Table 2, and every downstream claim survive unchanged, and no new lemma or global argument is required.

issues.failure_explanation: By eq:lap_pdf_as_exp and K_v(z) ~ sqrt(pi/(2z)) e^{-z} with v=(2-d)/2, the multivariate Laplace density satisfies \psi_{lap}(y) ~ C (y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y)^{(1-d)/4} exp(-sqrt(2 y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y)), so |r^{NIG}| ~ C' sqrt(det \tilde{\Sigma}) (y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y)^{(d-1)/4} exp( sqrt(2 y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y) - \delta T sqrt(y'\Delta y) ). The definition of h_1^{NIG} in eq:T_NIG drops the polynomial factor (y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y)^{(d-1)/4}. At the paper's own recommended choice \tilde{\Sigma} = (2/(\delta^2 T^2)) \Delta^{-1} the exponential terms cancel identically in every direction (up to o(1) in the exponent), so the limit is not sqrt(det \tilde{\Sigma}) as case (ii) claims: for d >= 2, h_1^{NIG} grows like (y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y)^{(d-1)/4} -> +\infty. Consequently the non-strict condition \delta^2 T^2 \Delta - 2\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1} \succeq 0 stated in Table tab:multivariate_dom_tranf, and the equality construction adopted in the text, do not control the boundary growth of the transformed integrand for d >= 2, violating the paper's own boundedness criterion. (For d=1 the exponent (d-1)/4 vanishes and the univariate analysis is correct.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the Bessel prefactor (y'\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1}y)^{(d-1)/4} in h_1^{NIG}, correct case (ii) to divergence for d >= 2, and impose the strict condition \delta^2 T^2 \Delta - 2\tilde{\Sigma}^{-1} \succ 0, e.g. \tilde{\Sigma} = (2(1+\epsilon)/(\delta^2 T^2)) \Delta^{-1} with \epsilon>0, under which the exponential decay dominates the polynomial factor and h_1^{NIG} -> 0; update Table tab:multivariate_dom_tranf and the adopted construction accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The multivariate (dependent-asset) NIG domain-transformation rule and its Table 2 condition are stated to keep the transformed integrand bounded at the corners of [0,1]^d; for d >= 2 the recommended choice instead yields polynomial boundary growth, so the stated regularity preservation underlying the near-optimal RQMC rate rationale is not achieved for the dependent NIG case (payoff-transform decay may still compensate in practice, but that is not the guarantee given). The GBM and VG rules and Propositions prop:vg_proposition and prop:nig_proposition are unaffected.
issues.title: Dropped Bessel prefactor invalidates the multivariate NIG critical case and the adopted transformation rule for d >= 2
issues.why_classification: The repair requires redoing the asymptotic analysis with the dropped prefactor and changing the advertised condition and the recommended construction (withdrawing the equality choice for d >= 2), which is more than a routine local fix; however, the strict-inequality variant is fully supported by the existing derivation and preserves the method, the convergence rates, and the advertised scope, so no new architecture or major loss results.
